title: Kernel lifecycle & cache-coordinator weekly note — capacity dance and batching experiments
content:
Goals this week:
- Stabilize kernel lifecycle transitions during sudden load swings (goal: reduce 99th P50 spikes caused by kernel swap).
- Validate cache-coordinator heuristics for short-lived sessions to avoid thrashing.
- Run three micro-batching scenarios to measure tail-latency vs. throughput tradeoffs.

Sprint highlights / quick summary:
- Observed a recurring pattern where inflight kernel offloads + aggressive eviction caused KV cache misses at the exact moment a cohort ramped up. Repro across two clusters (us-west-2 prod-sim).
- Cache-coordinator prototype (opt-ttl branch) reduced rewarm rate by ~18% for sessions <12s, but increased median token latency by 3ms due to extra coordination RPCs.
- Micro-batching experiment B (adaptive-window) increased throughput for medium-length requests (seq_len 512) by 12% and kept 95th latency within SLO. But 99th tail regressed in cross-tenant synthetic load.

Detailed notes / observations:
1) Kernel lifecycle edge: 
   - Root cause hypothesis: kernel swap triggers synchronous KV cache pointer invalidation that forces downstream prefill to run cold. When prefill traffic aligns with swap, we see tail spikes.
   - Evidence: spike correlation from traces (trace ids: 4ab2f, 7c9d1). Heap snapshots show active KV refs drop then reappear.
   - Discussion outcome: avoid synchronous pointer invalidation. Plan to introduce grace-window (200ms) and async pointer reclamation.

2) Cache-coordinator experiment (opt-ttl):
   - Mechanic: mark session keys with short adaptive TTL if session length estimate < 15s. Coordinator consolidates eviction decisions across kernels on same host.
   - Metrics: rewarm-rate down 18%, cache-hit rate improved +4pp for short sessions, RPC overhead +0.9 rps/core.
   - Tradeoffs: small latency tax (median +3ms) due to extra RPC and decision logic. Backend SRE ok with tradeoff for now.

3) Batching scenarios tested:
   - Baseline: current steady 32ms batching window.
   - Variant A (fixed-40ms): small throughput gain, tail same.
   - Variant B (adaptive-window): adapts window by arrival rate and seq_len; best throughput for seq_len 256-768, but under cross-tenant stress we observed queue inversion causing some long-waits at 99th.
   - Variant C (priority-slicing): short requests slice through with priority token; improved 99th for short requests but harmed mid-size throughput.

Decisions made:
- Merge cache-coordinator opt-ttl into an experimental toggle behind runtime flag (rollout to staging only). Owner: Diego. Target: feature-flag rollout by 2026-03-18. (JIRA:SRV-1307).
- Implement kernel pointer grace-window prototype (200ms) in kernel-swap flow. Owner: Priya. Prototype PR due 2026-03-17.
- Pause adaptive-window global rollout until queue-inversion sample size increases and we can add a fairness layer. Owner: Liam to capture fairness design.

Open questions / unresolved:
- Is the 200ms grace-window the right default across different GPU types (A100 vs H100)? Need perf matrix by hardware. (Action: Asha to coordinate perf runs).
- Can we tighten coordinator RPCs (reduce payload or batch decisions) to remove the 3ms median cost? Potential to move decisions to in-process host agent.
- How to detect in-run queue inversion earlier and fallback to fixed window without oscillation?

Actions & owners (short list):
- Diego: roll out opt-ttl to staging behind flag; collect 7d metrics; add dashboard tiles for rewarm-rate, RPC-per-decision. Due: 2026-03-18.
- Priya: open kernel-swap grace-window PR; include unit/benchmarks across seq_len 128/512/1024. Due: 2026-03-17.
- Liam: design fairness shim for adaptive-window; prototype algorithm notes in this doc. Due: 2026-03-20.
- Asha: run hardware matrix: A100/H100 (single and multi-tenant) for grace-window sensitivity. Due: 2026-03-21.
- Ops oncall: prepare rollback playbook for opt-ttl (link to runbook in Confluence). Due: 2026-03-18.

Risks / mitigation:
- Risk: opt-ttl flag could add RPC saturation in high-density hosts. Mitigation: set circuit-breaker, monitor RPC latency, auto-disable if >50ms avg.
- Risk: fairness shim adds scheduling overhead. Mitigate by sampling-based insertion and only enabling on hosts with >X queued requests.

Meeting minutes (2026-03-12 sync):
- Quick demos: Diego showed opt-ttl metric dashboard; Priya walked through pointer lifecycle.
- Consensus: move cautiously; prefer staged experiments with strong rollback criteria.

Notes to self / informal: 
- Remember to add trace tags for coordinator-decisions so we can filter traces quicker.
- Keep short-session heuristics conservative in first rollout.

Useful links / references: 
- PR: github.com/redwood/serving-runtime/pull/4129
- Jira: SRV-1245 (kernel-swap investigations), SRV-1307 (cache-coordinator opt-ttl)
- Slack: #runtime-kernel (thread ts: 1612345567.000200)

Next sync: Wednesday standup deep-dive (bring perf numbers for grace-window across hw types).

Attachments / artifacts to upload when ready: profiler snapshots, evictions trace slices, perf csvs.

-- Asha
